Summarize tumor-enriched splicing

Ryan Corbett

2025

This scripts identifies recurrent tumor-enriched junctions in primary PBTA tumors and generates summary plots by sample and tumor histology

Load required packages

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(qs2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(data.table)
  library(rprojroot)
  library(R.utils)
  library(ggsci)
  library(ggforce)
  library(ggpubr)
})

Set directory paths

root_dir <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_dir(".git"))
data_dir <- file.path(root_dir, "data")
analysis_dir <- file.path(root_dir, "analyses", "05-summarize-TEJs")
input_dir <- file.path(analysis_dir, "input")
results_dir <- file.path(analysis_dir, "results")
plot_dir <- file.path(analysis_dir, "plots")
if (!dir.exists(results_dir)) {
  dir.create(results_dir)
}

source(file.path(root_dir, "figures", "theme_for_plots.R"))

Set file paths

tej_file <- file.path(root_dir, "analyses",
                      "04-tej-differential-splicing",
                      "results",
                      "tumor-enriched-oncofetal-diff-splice-junctions.qs2")

hist_file <- file.path(root_dir, "analyses",
                       "00-create-cohort-histologies",
                       "results",
                       "cohort-histologies.tsv")

Wrangle data

tej_df <- qs2::qs_read(tej_file)

hist <- read_tsv(hist_file)

Filter TEJ df for samples in cohort hist, and append relevant metadata

tej_df <- tej_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(Kids_First_Biospecimen_ID %in% hist$Kids_First_Biospecimen_ID) %>%
  left_join(hist %>% 
              dplyr::select(Kids_First_Biospecimen_ID,
                            sample_type,
                            tumor_descriptor,
                            composition,
                            molecular_subtype,
                            RNA_library,
                            plot_group,
                            plot_group_hex),
            by = "Kids_First_Biospecimen_ID")

Filter TEJs for those in primary independent specimens

primary_independent_specimens <- hist %>%
  dplyr::filter(is_independent_primary == "Yes") %>%
  pull(Kids_First_Biospecimen_ID)

primary_tej_df <- tej_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(Kids_First_Biospecimen_ID %in% primary_independent_specimens)

Identify most recurrent exon-exon junction for each TEJ boundary (prioritizing those that are most recurrent in primary tumors), and filter full and primary df for these TEJs

# get most recurrent exon-exon jc for boundaries in primary tumors
top_primary_bounds <- primary_tej_df %>%
  # count TEJ N per boundary
  dplyr::count(boundary, junction) %>%
  # arrange in descending n order
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  # keep most prevalent TEJ per boundary
  distinct(boundary, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  pull(junction)

# for TEJs in non-primary tumors only, get most recurrent exon-exon jc
top_other_bounds <- tej_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(!boundary %in% primary_tej_df$boundary) %>%
  # count TEJ N per boundary
  dplyr::count(boundary, junction) %>%
  # arrange in descending n order
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  # keep most prevalent TEJ per boundary
  distinct(boundary, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  pull(junction)

# filter TEJ df
tej_df <- tej_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(junction %in% c(top_primary_bounds,
                                top_other_bounds)) 

# save to output
write_tsv(tej_df,
          file.path(results_dir,
                    "tumor-enriched-oncofetal-splice-junctions-cohort-filtered.tsv.gz"))

primary_tej_df <- primary_tej_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(junction %in% c(top_primary_bounds,
                                top_other_bounds))

Filter for recurrent events (i.e., event observed in >5% of tumor histologies)

# Get number of patients per histology
# n_per_hist <- hist %>%
#   dplyr::filter(is_independent_primary == "Yes") %>%
#   distinct(Kids_First_Biospecimen_ID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
#   count(plot_group) %>%
#   dplyr::rename(n_hist = n)

primary_tej_df <- primary_tej_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(plot_group_collapsed = case_when(
    plot_group %in% c("Other high-grade glioma",
                      "DIPG or DMG") ~ "HGG",
      TRUE ~ plot_group
  ))

# obtain frequency of splice events by hist
n_per_hist_jc <- primary_tej_df %>%
  count(plot_group_collapsed, junction) %>%
  dplyr::rename(n_hist_jc = n) %>%
  # filter for events in >=3 samples in histology
  dplyr::filter(n_hist_jc >= 3)

# retain only recurrent events
recurrent_primary_tej_df <- primary_tej_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(glue::glue("{plot_group_collapsed}-{junction}") %in% glue::glue("{n_per_hist_jc$plot_group_collapsed}-{n_per_hist_jc$junction}")) %>%
  dplyr::select(-plot_group_collapsed)

Plot total and recurrent tej n by histology

total_tej_hist_n <- primary_tej_df %>%
  distinct(plot_group, junction) %>%
  dplyr::count(plot_group) %>%
  dplyr::rename(total_tej_n = n)

recurrent_tej_hist_n <- recurrent_primary_tej_df %>%
  distinct(plot_group, junction) %>%
  dplyr::count(plot_group) %>%
  dplyr::rename(recurrent_tej_n = n) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(recurrent_tej_n)

# order based on N recurrent events
hist_order <- recurrent_tej_hist_n$plot_group

tej_n_plot_df <- total_tej_hist_n %>%
  left_join(recurrent_tej_hist_n) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(nonrecurrent_tej_n = total_tej_n - recurrent_tej_n) %>%
  dplyr::select(-total_tej_n) %>%
  pivot_longer(-plot_group,
               names_to = "tej_group",
               values_to = "n") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tej_group = case_when(
    tej_group == "recurrent_tej_n" ~ "Recurrent",
    tej_group == "nonrecurrent_tej_n" ~ "Non-recurrent"
  )) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(plot_group = fct_relevel(plot_group,
                                         hist_order)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(plot_group)
Joining with `by = join_by(plot_group)`
# generate plot
tej_n_barplot <- tej_n_plot_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(y = factor(plot_group), x = n, fill = tej_group)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black", show.legend = TRUE) + 
  scale_fill_npg() +
  theme_Publication() +
  labs(x = "N TEJs",
     y = NULL,
     fill = NULL)

# save to output
ggsave(file.path(plot_dir,
                 "tej-n-by-hist-barplot.pdf"),
       tej_n_barplot,
       width = 7, height = 6)

Assess recurrent TEJs for RNA library type bias

# A TEJ is absent from the input data when it was not called. Count all
# eligible primary samples by library class first, then join observed calls
# to those denominators. This retains TEJ-negative samples without creating
# a very large sample-by-junction matrix.
library_type_samples <- hist %>%
  dplyr::filter(is_independent_primary == "Yes",
                RNA_library %in% c("stranded", "poly-A", "poly-A stranded")) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Kids_First_Biospecimen_ID,
    RNA_library_class = dplyr::if_else(RNA_library == "stranded",
                                        "total_RNA", "polyA")
  ) %>%
  distinct(Kids_First_Biospecimen_ID, .keep_all = TRUE)

library_type_denominators <- library_type_samples %>%
  count(RNA_library_class, name = "n_samples")

recurrent_junctions <- recurrent_primary_tej_df %>%
  distinct(junction) %>%
  pull(junction)

called_recurrent_tejs <- recurrent_primary_tej_df %>%
  distinct(Kids_First_Biospecimen_ID, junction) %>%
  inner_join(library_type_samples,
             by = "Kids_First_Biospecimen_ID") %>%
  count(junction, RNA_library_class, name = "n_called")

# Every junction is represented in both library classes; missing values after
# the join are therefore genuine zero-call classes.
library_bias_input <- tidyr::crossing(
  junction = recurrent_junctions,
  library_type_denominators
) %>%
  left_join(called_recurrent_tejs,
            by = c("junction", "RNA_library_class")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(n_called = tidyr::replace_na(n_called, 0L),
                RNA_library_class = factor(RNA_library_class,
                                           levels = c("total_RNA", "polyA")))

# First, report the directly interpretable frequency in each library class.
library_bias_summary <- library_bias_input %>%
  group_by(junction, RNA_library_class) %>%
  summarise(n_samples = sum(n_samples),
            n_called = sum(n_called),
            call_frequency = n_called / n_samples,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = RNA_library_class,
              values_from = c(n_samples, n_called, call_frequency))

# Test each junction once for an association between calling and library class.
# An odds ratio >1 means a TEJ was called more often in total-RNA than in
# poly-A libraries.
test_library_bias <- function(event_df) {
  if (nrow(event_df) != 2 ||
      sum(event_df$n_called) == 0 ||
      sum(event_df$n_called) == sum(event_df$n_samples)) {
    return(tibble(odds_ratio_total_RNA_vs_polyA = NA_real_,
                  conf_low = NA_real_,
                  conf_high = NA_real_,
                  p_value = NA_real_))
  }

  event_df <- event_df %>% dplyr::arrange(RNA_library_class)
  # Rows encode called then absent and columns are total-RNA then poly-A,
  # so the odds ratio is in the total-RNA/poly-A direction.
  fisher_table <- rbind(event_df$n_called,
                        event_df$n_samples - event_df$n_called)
  fisher <- stats::fisher.test(fisher_table)

  tibble(odds_ratio_total_RNA_vs_polyA = unname(fisher$estimate),
         conf_low = unname(fisher$conf.int[1]),
         conf_high = unname(fisher$conf.int[2]),
         p_value = fisher$p.value)
}

library_bias_results <- library_bias_input %>%
  group_by(junction) %>%
  group_modify(~ test_library_bias(.x)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")) %>%
  left_join(library_bias_summary, by = "junction") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    library_bias = case_when(
      p_adj < 0.05 & odds_ratio_total_RNA_vs_polyA >= 2 ~ "total_RNA",
      p_adj < 0.05 & odds_ratio_total_RNA_vs_polyA <= 0.5 ~ "polyA",
      TRUE ~ "none"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(p_adj, desc(abs(log2(odds_ratio_total_RNA_vs_polyA))))

write_tsv(library_bias_results,
          file.path(results_dir, "recurrent-tej-rna-library-bias.tsv.gz"))

# Append the per-junction library-bias results to every corresponding
# sample-level recurrent TEJ record before the final recurrent-TEJ export.
recurrent_primary_tej_df <- recurrent_primary_tej_df %>%
  left_join(library_bias_results, by = "junction")

# This plot is useful for inspecting effect size and avoiding interpretation
# of statistically significant but very small frequency differences.
library_bias_plot <- library_bias_results %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = call_frequency_polyA,
             y = call_frequency_total_RNA,
             color = library_bias)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(total_RNA = "#0072B2",
                                polyA = "#D55E00",
                                none = "grey70")) +
  theme_Publication() +
  labs(x = "TEJ call frequency in poly-A libraries",
       y = "TEJ call frequency in total-RNA libraries",
       color = "Library bias")

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "recurrent-tej-rna-library-bias.pdf"),
       library_bias_plot, width = 5, height = 5)

library_bias_results %>%
  dplyr::filter(library_bias != "none")

Plot distribution of TEJ splice event types by histology

recurrent_primary_tej_df <- recurrent_primary_tej_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(preference_code = case_when(
    consensus_jc_event_type == "exon skipping" ~ "ES",
    consensus_jc_event_type == "exon inclusion" ~ "EI",
    consensus_jc_event_type == "intron retention" ~ "RI",
    consensus_jc_event_type == "A3SS+" ~ "A3+",
    consensus_jc_event_type == "A3SS-" ~ "A3-",
    consensus_jc_event_type == "A5SS+" ~ "A5+",
    consensus_jc_event_type == "A5SS-" ~ "A5-"
  ))

# define tumor preference palette
preference_palette <- c("EI" = "#56B4E9",
                        "ES" = "#0072B2",
                        "RI" = "#009E73",
                        "A3-" = "#E69F00",
                        "A3+" = "#F0E442",
                        "A5-" = "#D55E00",
                        "A5+" = "#CC79A7")

unique_hist_event_ct <- recurrent_primary_tej_df %>%
  distinct(plot_group, junction) %>%
  dplyr::count(plot_group) %>%
  dplyr::rename(hist_event_n = n)

hist_event_type_ct <- recurrent_primary_tej_df %>%
  distinct(junction, plot_group, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::count(plot_group, preference_code) %>%
  left_join(unique_hist_event_ct) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(n_norm = n/hist_event_n)
Joining with `by = join_by(plot_group)`
event_type_freq_barplot <- hist_event_type_ct %>%
